name: Regulatory filings and returns
one_line: Documents an entity (or a person acting for one) is REQUIRED to submit to an authority or registry, and the authority's responses: annual confirmations and returns, registry forms and change notifications, sector returns, beneficial-ownership and officer filings, submission receipts, acknowledgements, certificates, and penalty or reminder notices. The anchor is an OBLIGATION TO AN AUTHORITY with a deadline and a filing reference — a document whose existence is compelled from outside. Absorbs the legacy row corp.regulatory-filings. Gist-level placeholder (J-IND): it recognises the situation and writes NO field rows, because the business_operations schema declares none.

deterministic: PRECONDITION: every entry below is a DETECTION signal and never an extraction licence. The business_operations schema declares no field rows (D1 as narrowed, _CONTRACT rules 10 and 15, CONNECTION PR-6), so nothing here writes a domain fact; detection exists so the material is recognised, kept where this row's sensitivity says, and offered honestly. “Privacy policy must be enforced before content reaches any model or external connector.”

an authority-return structure: a form whose issuing body is a registry, revenue authority, or sector regulator, with a labelled entity-identifier slot, a labelled period or as-at-date slot, and a declaration or signature block. The issuing body is matched at a word boundary against R4's gazetteer content; R4 owns the gazetteer and this row writes no names.

a submission-receipt structure: an acknowledgement carrying a submission reference, a received timestamp, a form or return name, and the submitting entity's identifier — generated by the authority's system and unmistakably machine-issued.
a registry-certificate structure: incorporation, change of name, dissolution or registration certificates carrying a registry seal or crest, a registered number, and an effective date.
a compelled-notice structure: a reminder, penalty, or enquiry notice from an authority carrying a case or reference number, a statutory deadline, and a consequence statement.

a labelled machine-return payload — a structured return file (an XML or a fixed-schema export) whose root element or header names a return type and a period. The payload is a labelled slot, not a format claim: “treat the file extension as a routing signal rather than an assumption about meaning”

a deadline structure: a filing calendar or obligations schedule listing return names against statutory due dates and responsible parties. “Tables matter because resumes, forms, applications, invoices, and administrative documents often place their most useful information in cells rather than body paragraphs.”
an email whose labelled sender slot resolves to an authority or filing-agent domain and whose labelled subject slot names a return, a reference, or a deadline.
parent-folder context naming an authority, a return type, or a filing year, treated as a clue once one of the structures above is present. Folder context never fires alone.
needs_llm: PRECONDITION: this world is commercially confidential and often confidential to a THIRD party, so any model step runs after P7 and under the user's policy. “Protected material should not be included in cloud-model prompts by default, should not display raw content in general group summaries, and should not be moved automatically without a user policy that explicitly permits it.”

separating a COMPELLED submission from a voluntary one and from an application. A grant application, a permit application and a tender are addressed to authorities too; only the obligation makes a return.

separating an ENTITY's filing from a PERSON's. Self-assessment returns, personal registrations and sole-trader filings are made by individuals for themselves and belong with the person's own finance and identity material, which is safety-domain territory.
separating a real filed return from a draft, a working copy, a filing agent's template and a blank statutory form.

reading a jurisdiction's return correctly at all when its vocabulary is not in the deterministic catalogue — this row is the most jurisdiction-shaped in the family, and per D4 what varies is VALUES, never field names.
unlabelled correspondence with an authority: a covering letter, an extension request, a chasing note with no reference.
in every case above, abstention is the required outcome where the evidence does not settle it. “A model that cannot cite sufficient evidence must return unknown.”
never_alone: an authority or registry gazetteer hit alone. An authority name appears on published guidance, on marketing material citing regulation, on a job description, and in a news article, and this is the tempting false file for this row.
regulatory vocabulary alone — return, filing, submission, compliance, statutory, deadline. Accountancy firms' newsletters and saved guidance PDFs are dense in it.

a reference-shaped or number-shaped token alone. Registration numbers, tax references, case numbers and invoice numbers are indistinguishable without a labelled slot, and a bare 4-digit run is not a period.

a period-shaped token alone, read as a tax year. A registry period, a fiscal year, an academic year and a calendar year all present identically, and asserting `tax_year` would quietly claim they coincide.

a company, charity, or regulator gazetteer hit alone. 00 states the ambiguity for a university — “A university name alone should not create a group because Columbia can appear as an authoring school, course provider, target institution, employer, research venue, or merely a cited organization.” — and a company name is worse, appearing as employer, customer, supplier, competitor, regulator, and as the letterhead of a document that is merely ABOUT the holder. Stated as inference; 00 writes that sentence about a university, not a company.

source_type or extension alone. “treat the file extension as a routing signal rather than an assumption about meaning”, and file_kind_plausible is constitutionally never-alone (CONNECTION section 5, invariant 2).
membership in a download session that emptied a document-management system or a mail thread's attachments at once. “A session should never be treated as proof of topic”

a PDF author, producer, or company metadata string alone. “PDF metadata should be treated as supporting evidence, not as truth” — a corporate template stamps the same entity on every blank form it ever generated.
a bare 4-digit number read as a fiscal year, an entity number, a contract number, or a document version.

work_types: registry change notification (officers, address, capital, name)
grouping_reasons: one filing occurrence: the prepared return, the supporting schedules, the submission receipt and the authority's acknowledgement — purpose-coherent even where the members share no content. “The documents are content-incoherent but purpose-coherent.”
one return type across its periods, joined by a return name and an entity identifier rather than by filenames.

one entity's whole registry history: incorporation, changes, annual filings, certificates. This is a real reason to group and the one most likely to tempt an entity label onto an unrelated PDF carrying the same company name, which is exactly what must not happen. “The graph does not automatically copy those missing facts onto sparse files.”
one deadline event: the reminder, the preparation, the submission and the receipt.
no group at all is a valid outcome: an isolated certificate is an ordinary standalone record and 00's residual library exists for it.

and the stop rules apply as written — “when members carry irreconcilable course, institution, project, term, or purpose facts” — two entities' returns in one folder do not merge, and this is the row where that most often matters because one person files for several entities.

template.why: Empty by binding contract: a dimension may only branch on a field the same entry's schema declares, and business_operations declares none (D1 as narrowed, _CONTRACT rules 10 and 15, CONNECTION PR-6). That is a contract fact, not a claim that this situation has no shape — it plainly does, and it is recorded here as PROSE for whoever answers the schema row's open_question. The recommendation, held as prose: the entity whose obligation it is — here the entity level is NOT a vanity collector, because a person who files for two companies genuinely needs it as the top separator — then the authority or return type, then the period, then the document function (return / receipt / certificate / notice). The period is more load-bearing here than anywhere else in the family, but it still is not first. Not time-first — “For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders.” And whatever eventually lands stays a recommendation: “The system recommends an order based on the domain template, but the user can reverse, remove, add, or flatten dimensions.”

collides_with.signal: The load-bearing collision on this row and a live edge of NJ-J-IND-3. A tax return is a compelled submission to an authority (this row) and a custodial financial record (the finance safety schema's row) at once, and the same PDF is both. The discriminating evidence: an entity identifier, a registry or regulator framing and a corporate return name lean to this row; a personal tax reference, an individual filer, or a supporting statement set leans to the finance row — which is a safety row, so where they co-activate the protective ordering runs first. Provenance: inference.

Filings and compliance evidence are prepared by the same people for the same deadlines. The discriminating evidence: a submission to a named authority with a filing reference and an acknowledgement supports this row; a control, a finding, or an assessor's report supports the audit row. Provenance: inference.

An authority's own record of a return and the filer's copy are the same document. The discriminating evidence is which side the holder is on: a statutory power, a case-handling framing, or an issuing letterhead written FROM the authority supports the government row; a submitted return and a received acknowledgement held by the filer supports this row. Provenance: inference.

Permits, licences and their renewals are also authority documents with references and deadlines. The discriminating evidence: an application for a permission, a conditions schedule, or a licence certificate supports the permit row; a periodic compelled return with no permission sought supports this row. Provenance: inference.

A practitioner filing on a client's behalf produces byte-identical returns and receipts. The discriminating evidence: a matter identifier, an engagement framing, a filed-by-agent authorisation held as the agent's own record, or a time-recording anchor supports law_practice; the same return held by the entity it is ABOUT supports this row. Provenance: inference.

Officer appointments, registry changes and confirmation statements are the corporate-secretarial function's ordinary output, whether in-house or outsourced. The discriminating evidence is the same matter-and-engagement anchor. Provenance: inference.

Charity annual returns, trustee filings and regulator correspondence are this row's shape with a different registry. The discriminating evidence is owner type: a charity or association registration slot and a trustee framing supports nonprofit; a company registration and a commercial framing supports this row. Provenance: inference.

Share allotments, transfers and capital reductions are simultaneously registry filings and cap-table events. The discriminating evidence: a statutory form and a submission receipt support this row; a share register, a shareholder agreement, or an option-grant record supports the cap-table row. Provenance: inference.

Sector regulated returns — generation, abstraction, emissions, metering — carry a period, an authority and a submission reference exactly as here. The discriminating evidence is a site, an asset, or a metered-quantity anchor, which supports the sector row. Provenance: inference.

falls_through_to.why: The commonest home for a filed return, a certificate, an acknowledgement or a notice with no group around it — this row's members are unusually often genuinely standalone. “Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group.”

Where a filing carries an individual's date of birth, address or personal reference, or where the entity's affairs are not public, the protective home is correct. “Protected Records may represent sensitive isolated material such as passport scans, medical documents, account statements, visas, legal forms, or credentials; it should normally remain local-only and must not cause filenames or content to be exposed in model prompts.”

The honest outcome where the entity or the authority cannot be resolved from the file itself — frequent where one person files for several entities. “Review Later may hold files whose meaning is partly understood but whose final location requires a future decision.”

An isolated submission receipt with no return around it is exactly a transactional confirmation. “Receipts and Confirmations may hold isolated invoices, delivery confirmations, booking records, boarding passes, purchase receipts, event tickets, and similar transactional documents.”

Published authority guidance and accountancy newsletters are the tempting false files of this row. “Reading Inbox may hold papers, articles, reports, and saved PDFs that appear to be reading material but have no active research, course, or project association.”

Structured return payloads and password-protected filing bundles are ordinary here and are safest represented without moving. “Unsupported or Encrypted may hold—or, more safely, represent without moving—password-protected archives, unreadable documents, damaged files, and unknown formats.”

sensitivity_why: Two grounds. First, this row's forms routinely carry an identifiable individual's date of birth, residential or service address and personal tax reference — officer appointments and beneficial-ownership statements exist to record exactly that — and 00 names the class in its corpus sentence: the corpus “can include identity documents, account statements, tax records, medical information, legal records, credentials, private correspondence, GPS metadata, employment materials, and educational records”, and requires the immediate transition for such material: “A scanned passport, tax statement, medical document, authentication key, or account record should enter a protected state immediately.” Second, as inference: the fact that a registry PUBLISHES some of this does not make the holder's own copy safe to expose, because the copy sits beside drafts, workings and correspondence that were never published. This row assigns only the catalogue value potentially_sensitive; the handling class is P7's and is not set here.
open_question: Two. (1) NJ-J-IND-3 in its most literal form: a corporate tax return is simultaneously this row's compelled filing and the finance safety schema's custodial record, and the roster's split sends corp.regulatory-filings here while sending corporate accounting to finance. That boundary was drawn by the roster pass, not by 00, and this row cannot settle it. (2) This is the most jurisdiction-shaped row in the family. D4 is ratified — jurisdiction is a VALUE, never a field name and never a destination dimension — so the correct consequence is that R4's gazetteers and R5's one jurisdiction's values carry every authority and return name, and that this row deliberately names none. Whether the v1 gazetteer covers enough authorities for this row to fire at all is a P10 planning question, not this row's.
